beats.caption: This is Planet Quiz: a solar system trivia app that runs a language model on your own laptop.
beats.say: This is Planet Quiz: a solar system trivia app that runs a language model on your own laptop.

beats.caption: In the next few minutes you will learn what RAG is, how its pipeline works, and exactly how this project uses it.
beats.say: In the next few minutes you will learn what RAG is, how its pipeline works, and exactly how this project uses it.

beats.caption: A language model is trained once. After that, its knowledge is frozen.
beats.say: Start with the problem. A language model is trained once. After that, its knowledge is frozen.

beats.caption: When you ask a question, it does not look anything up. It predicts the most likely next words from memory.
beats.say: When you ask it a question, it does not look anything up. It predicts the most likely next words, from memory.

beats.caption: We asked our local model how many moons Saturn has. One run said 83. Another run said 146.
beats.say: We asked our local model how many moons Saturn has. One run said eighty-three. Another run said one hundred and forty-six.

beats.caption: Three problems: the answer may be out of date, it may be made up (a hallucination), and you cannot check where it came from.
beats.say: That gives us three problems. The answer may be out of date. It may be made up, which is called a hallucination. And you cannot check where it came from.

beats.caption: RAG stands for retrieval-augmented generation.
beats.say: RAG stands for retrieval augmented generation.

beats.caption: Think of an open-book exam: the model first gets the relevant pages, and then answers from those pages.
beats.say: Think of an open-book exam. Instead of answering from memory, the model first gets the relevant pages, and then answers from those pages.

beats.caption: Retrieval: find the passages that match the question.
beats.say: Three words, three steps. Retrieval: find the passages that match the question.

beats.caption: Augmented: paste those passages into the prompt. Generation: the model writes the answer from them.
beats.say: Augmented: paste those passages into the prompt. Generation: the model writes the answer from them.

beats.caption: RAG does not retrain the model. The weights stay the same. Only the input changes.
beats.say: One thing is important to remember. RAG does not retrain the model. The weights stay exactly the same. Only the input changes.

beats.caption: A RAG system has two phases. Indexing happens once: we turn our documents into a searchable store.
beats.say: A RAG system has two phases. Indexing happens once, before anyone asks anything. We turn our documents into a searchable store.

beats.caption: Answering happens on every question.
beats.say: Answering happens on every question.

beats.caption: The sources: two PDF files from 2013, a NASA fact sheet set and a brochure from the German Aerospace Center. 142 pages in total.
beats.say: Indexing starts with the sources. We use two P D F files from twenty thirteen: a NASA fact sheet set, and a brochure from the German Aerospace Center. One hundred and forty-two pages in total.

beats.caption: Step 1, extraction: a library called PyMuPDF pulls the text out of each page.
beats.say: Step one is extraction. A library called Pie M U P D F pulls the text out of each page.

beats.caption: Step 2, cleaning: repair words split across lines, and drop pages with almost no text. 119 pages remain.
beats.say: Step two is cleaning. We repair words that were split across lines, and we drop pages with almost no text, like covers. One hundred and nineteen pages remain.

beats.caption: Step 3, chunking: cut the text into chunks of about 1,000 characters, because a whole page is too big and too mixed to search well.
beats.say: Step three is chunking. A whole page is too big and too mixed to search well, so we cut the text into chunks of about one thousand characters.

beats.caption: Neighbouring chunks overlap by 150 characters, so a sentence at the border is not cut in half. Result: 532 chunks.
beats.say: Neighbouring chunks overlap by one hundred and fifty characters, so a sentence at the border is not cut in half. That gives five hundred and thirty-two chunks.

beats.caption: Step 4, embedding: an embedding model turns each chunk into a long list of numbers, called a vector.
beats.say: Step four is embedding. An embedding model turns each chunk into a long list of numbers, called a vector.

beats.caption: Texts with similar meaning get vectors that point in similar directions.
beats.say: Texts with similar meaning get vectors that point in similar directions.

beats.caption: Step 5, storing: every vector is saved with its text and page number in a vector database called Chroma.
beats.say: Step five is storing. Every vector is saved, together with its text and page number, in a vector database called Chroma.

beats.caption: In our project all of this is one file, app/ingest.py, and you run it once.
beats.say: In our project, all of this is one file, ingest dot pie, and you run it once.

beats.caption: Someone asks: how many moons does Saturn have? The question goes through the same embedding model and becomes a vector too.
beats.say: Now someone asks: how many moons does Saturn have? The question goes through the same embedding model, so it becomes a vector too.

beats.caption: Chroma compares the question vector with all 532 chunk vectors.
beats.say: Chroma compares the question vector with all five hundred and thirty-two chunk vectors.

beats.caption: The measure is cosine similarity: the smaller the angle between two vectors, the closer the meaning. We keep the top 4 chunks.
beats.say: The measure is called cosine similarity. The smaller the angle between two vectors, the closer the meaning. We keep the top four chunks.

beats.caption: Those four passages are numbered and placed in the prompt, together with the question and our instructions.
beats.say: Those four passages are numbered, and placed in the prompt, together with the question and our instructions.

beats.caption: The local model, Gemma 3 with 4 billion parameters, running in Ollama, reads the prompt and writes the answer.
beats.say: The local model, Gemma three, with four billion parameters, running in Ollama, reads the prompt and writes the answer.

beats.caption: It cites the passage numbers, and the app shows those passages next to the answer, so you can check it.
beats.say: It cites the passage numbers, and the app shows those passages next to the answer, so you can check it.

chapters.title: Where it lives in our code

beats.caption: ingest.py builds the index. rag.py does retrieval and calls the model.
beats.say: Here is where each step lives in our code. Ingest dot pie builds the index. Rag dot pie does retrieval, and calls the model.

beats.caption: prompts.py holds the instructions. main.py is the web server, and one HTML page is the user interface.
beats.say: Prompts dot pie holds the instructions. Main dot pie is the web server, and one H T M L page is the user interface.

beats.caption: LangChain gives us the building blocks: a PDF loader, a text splitter, the embedding and chat clients for Ollama, and the Chroma store.
beats.say: We did not write the plumbing ourselves. Lang Chain gives us the building blocks: a P D F loader, a text splitter, the embedding and chat clients for Ollama, and the Chroma store.

beats.caption: The instructions follow the 4T's. Traits: who the model is. A careful tutor that uses only the numbered passages.
beats.say: The instructions follow the four T's. Traits: who the model is. A careful tutor, that uses only the numbered passages.

beats.caption: Task: what to do. Answer the question and cite the passages.
beats.say: Task: what to do. Answer the question, and cite the passages.

beats.caption: Tone: encouraging and concise. Target: students aged 12 to 18, in at most four sentences.
beats.say: Tone: encouraging and concise. Target: students aged twelve to eighteen, in at most four sentences.

beats.caption: Small words matter. We first called the model a quiz master, and it added its own quiz question to every answer. Calling it a tutor fixed that.
beats.say: Small words matter. We first called the model a quiz master, and it started adding its own quiz question to every answer. Calling it a tutor fixed that.

beats.caption: Here is the app. In Ask mode, one button runs the same question twice: with retrieval, and without.
beats.say: Here is the app. In Ask mode, one button runs the same question twice: with retrieval, and without.

beats.caption: With RAG: 53 known moons, taken from the 2013 sources, with the source passages listed below.
beats.say: With RAG, the answer is fifty-three known moons, taken from the twenty thirteen sources, with the source passages listed below.

beats.caption: Without RAG, the model says 83, from memory.

beats.caption: 53 is no longer true today. RAG makes the model faithful to its sources, not correct about the world.
beats.say: Notice that fifty-three is no longer true today. RAG makes the model faithful to its sources, not correct about the world.

beats.caption: The quality of your documents becomes the quality of your answers.
beats.say: The quality of your documents becomes the quality of your answers.

beats.caption: Quiz mode uses the same retrieval: the model writes a question from two retrieved passages.
beats.say: Quiz mode uses the same retrieval. The model writes a question from two retrieved passages.

beats.caption: The player answers in free text, and the model grades the answer against the reference answer.
beats.say: The player answers in free text, and the model grades the answer against the reference answer.

beats.caption: RAG is not the right tool for everything. In a separate experiment we predicted how long a body takes to orbit the Sun, from its distance.
beats.say: RAG is not the right tool for everything. In a separate experiment, we predicted how long a body takes to orbit the Sun, from its distance.

beats.caption: A linear regression on a log scale was off by 0.02 years on average. The language model with RAG was off by almost 39 years.
beats.say: A linear regression on a log scale was off by zero point zero two years on average. The language model with RAG was off by almost thirty-nine years.

beats.caption: Retrieval finds similar text, not nearby numbers, and the model does not calculate.
beats.say: Retrieval finds similar text, not nearby numbers. And the model does not calculate.

beats.caption: Use RAG when the answer is a fact you can quote from a document. Use a trained model when the answer is a number that follows a pattern.
beats.say: So: use RAG when the answer is a fact you can quote from a document. Use a trained model when the answer is a number that follows a pattern.

beats.caption: RAG has limits. If retrieval misses the right passage, the answer is wrong or empty. A small model can still misread a passage. Every answer takes several seconds on a laptop.
beats.say: RAG also has limits. If retrieval misses the right passage, the answer will be wrong or empty. A small model can still misread a passage. And every answer takes several seconds on a laptop.
